name: inspect_python_pyc
description: Inspect one explicit local CPython 3.7–3.13 .pyc file with a supported 16-byte header without executing bytecode, invoking CPython or recovering source. Returns the header (magic, pinned python_version, PEP 552 flags, source hash or mtime/size), the top-level code object with nested functions, names, const summaries, and bytecode length/SHA-256. Complete output is the default. detail summary retains the complete Evidence and returns header/coverage. Include an optional python-pyc code_objects view to return selected names/indices/fields in the first call; inspect_analysis_view pages the same retained source later. Every matching display name survives under its parent-scoped source_index; nested_code represents code-constant references, not runtime calls. Marshal is walked with object, depth and string budgets; unsupported magics/layouts, truncated streams and exhausted budgets return no partial success. A recognized 3.14 (3627) or 3.15 (3666) magic is qualified from its packed 16-byte header — the refusal names the observed version and flags — but no marshal code layout is pinned for those versions, so no code object is reported. A decoded header is not proof the matching .py is present. Portable on supported Node hosts; no Python installation required.

parameters.description: Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.

max_depth.description: Maximum marshal nesting depth; exceeding the budget fails without partial success

max_file_bytes.description: Maximum selected file size in bytes; exceeding the budget fails without partial success

max_objects.description: Maximum marshal objects to examine; exceeding the budget fails without partial success

max_string_bytes.description: Maximum bytes retained for one marshal string or byte string; exceeding the budget fails without partial success

path.description: Absolute filesystem path to the selected CPython .pyc file
